summary: Named 47 of 58 FUN_XXXX functions in wmele.ovr via Ghidra annotations (SourceType.USER_DEFINED). wmele.ovr is the melee-combat overlay: it owns game states 0x0a (combat init), 0x0b (per-round redraw), and 0x0e (end-of-round cleanup / transition). Coverage spans the full combat lifecycle: encounter setup (monster-group spawn from monster-type templates, party-into-combat-slots copy, recursive group expansion), per-round resolution (rank/file assignment, attack-target rolling, attack-animation queue with depth-sorted insertion, per-slot status-effect decay, party-member damage/death, XP/treasure awards), the 3D combat-scene viewport renderer (a 2192-byte function that reuses the maze-walk position state to draw the dungeon walls behind the monster sprites, then overlays the monster placements via 11-byte slot records at 0x51a8), and the surrounding UI (window create/destroy, party panel redraw, flee attempt, sound effect playback). 11 functions remain as FUN_XXXX: 7 are tiny per-depth render flag-clearers (0x42a3 / 0x4306 / 0x4337 / 0x4368 / 0x4395 / 0x43c7 / 0x43f9 — each ~50 bytes, gated on the `0x513e..0x5140` per-depth bit flags, but their specific 'which piece of the combat-scene frame' role is too granular to name without dynamic-trace context), plus a few jump-table fragments Ghidra mis-identified as functions (0x4426 dispatches via an out-of-segment jump table at -0x760e).
method: PyGhidra + DecompInterface for all 58 functions. For each: extracted (a) decompiled C, (b) outgoing CALL edges (intra-overlay FUN_XXXX + indirect func_0x0000XXXX BSS thunks), (c) scalar operand values, (d) BSS data references. Thunks resolved via the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset); resolved 44 distinct thunks across 122 call sites. Names applied when there was multi-signal evidence: distinctive BSS field access patterns matching the combat-slot layout (0x43a8[i]+0x2c stride, slot fields at +0x2/+0x4 HP, +0x6/+0x8 SP, +0x22 status_level, +0x2a rank-file code, +0x18c..+0x195 status-timer arrays), unique state-transition writes to 0x363a, clear loops over the 7 monster-group / 12 animation-slot / 5-rank x 2-file tables. The maze-traversal helpers (0x2f8b, 0x2fc8, 0x30ee, 0x3153, 0x31b8, 0x3239, 0x3622, 0x37df) are byte-equivalent to the wmaze.ovr renderer's wall-check + step-by-facing helpers (0x357a, 0x35b7, 0xf2a, 0x36dd, 0x3742, 0x37a7) — they're reused for the combat-scene background view of the same map cell.

transitions_out: state 0xb: written by 0x2d6d (after init) and by 0x2ceb (when combat continues)
state 0x8: written by 0x1716 when entire party dies (party-wipe transition)
state 0x17: written by 0x1716 when 0x4356 (combat-end flag) is set by escape/victory paths
state from 0x4fce: written by 0x2ceb on combat-end (escape/victory transitions to caller's choice)

key_discoveries: wmele.ovr has a 14-byte overlay header (matches wbase.ovr, differs from winit.ovr's 12-byte). Dispatch entry at file offset 0x0e: clears 3 BSS flags (0x500e, 0x5010, 0x5012), then sequentially tests *0x363a == 0xa → calls 0x2d6d, == 0xe → calls 0x2ceb, == 0xb → calls 0x2b6a. Returns ax=0.

Combat slot layout (0x2c bytes each, 13 slots per group at 0x43a8[group]+slot*0x2c): +0x00 hp_max, +0x02 hp_cur, +0x04 sp_max_a (e.g. mage), +0x06 sp_cur_a, +0x08 sp_max_b (e.g. priest), +0x0a..0x17 (10 bytes) status-effect timer array, +0x10 'attacking' flag, +0x11 paralysis-ish flag, +0x13 some-status flag, +0x16 ?, +0x19a monster_type_id, +0x19b zone-resolved monster idx, +0x19c is_first_round, +0x19d slot_count_in_group, +0x18c..0x195 per-group status-timer arrays, +0x22 status_level (0..5), +0x23 secondary status flag, +0x24 turn-skip counter, +0x26/+0x27/+0x29 ambush damage flags, +0x29 attack target rank, +0x2a rank*10+file (0..0x4F, 0xff=unassigned), +0x2b some flee/fled flag.

Monster type layout (0xde bytes each, loaded via 0xc31e thunk into *0x43b6[i]): +0x74/+0x76 group-size dice (XdY format), +0x78/+0x7a hp-dice, +0x7c/+0x7e sp-dice, +0xa4/+0xa6 secondary-spawn type+chance, +0xa8 group-size-modifier divisor, +0xaa/+0xab speed-boost bytes, +0xc4 attack-damage-by-round table (4 bytes), +0xd1 zone-roll dice, +0xd2 sound-id-on-spawn, +0xd6 attack-count modifier, +0xd7 base attack count, +0xdc/+0xda special-zone-flags, +0x74 zone-spawn-count.

3D combat-scene viewport (renderer at 0x44e8, 2192 bytes — same size as wmaze.ovr's view_render_corridor_frame at 0x4ad7) reuses the maze-state globals (0x4f9a facing, 0x4f9c..0x4fa0 z/y/x, 0x4faa maze-data ptr) AND has its own combat-only renderer state at 0x5118 (current depth iter), 0x52f6 (active depth count, default 4), 0x52f2/0x52f4 (L/R parity flags), 0x51a8+i*0xb (monster placement records: byte +0x0/+0x2/+0x4/+0x6 are sprite ptrs L/R/back/forward; +0xa is depth idx; +0xb is some 0xff marker). Calls FUN_3239/FUN_3622/FUN_37df for front/left/right walls and FUN_3a7d/FUN_3fc5/FUN_41b4 to actually emit the wall/door descriptors via video_descriptor_render (0xf148 thunk).

Combat windows: 0x438a (left party panel, 0x13 wide x 0xb tall at (0,0x13)), 0x438c (right monster panel, 0x14 wide x 0xa tall at (0x14,0x13)). These hold the message scroll on left and the monster portrait area on right. Created in 0x2d6d, destroyed in 0x2a52.

The state-0xa handler 0x2d6d allocates 7 group descriptors + 12 animation slots up-front via the 0xf4be thunk (wroot 0x3a22, likely a per-overlay arena malloc — matches its use across all overlays for fresh allocations).

Sound: 0x008d loads + decompresses a SOUND%02d.SND file inline (filename built via 0x0cd6 boot_build_prompt_message — that's actually the generic 'load file by template' wroot helper). Plays via the global 'play sound' path (0xc546, the *ui_animation_helper / play-sound thunk). 0x008d is called from 0x401 (spawn) and 0x1010 (refresh) when monster type has a sound-id at +0xd2.

Recursive group spawn: 0x401 recursively spawns up to 5 monster groups (one per recursion depth). Each spawn rolls a 'secondary-spawn-chance' from the monster type at +0xa4..+0xa7 and if it triggers, recursively calls 0x401 with the secondary type's ID. Depth cap is (current_zone+1)/2 + 1 (+ 1 more if 0x4338 is non-zero). 100/150/75 for normal/ambush/party-surprise.

Rank/file occupancy at 0x4362 is a 2x5 (rank x file) array of 2-byte 'group index' entries (0x14 bytes total, cleared in 0x024d). 0x50b4 is a parallel 'is-attacking-this-turn' bitmap (also 2x5). 0x4348+i*5 and 0x433e+i*5 are per-rank-file attack target overrides (mage targeting hit dice etc.).

findings.claim: wmele.ovr has 14-byte header. Dispatch entry at file offset 0x0e handles game-state values 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e by calling 0x2d6d, 0x2b6a, 0x2ceb respectively.

evidence.details: ndisasm at file offset 0x0e shows: clear 0x500e/0x5010/0x5012, then three back-to-back `cmp word [0x363a], <N>; jnz; call <handler>` sequences for N=0xa,0xe,0xb. Header bytes 0x00..0x0d are F2 00 72 45 D9 4D EE 4F 20 00 F4 02 E8 92 (overlay link table). Matches wbase.ovr header style. State transitions: 0x2d6d→0xb; 0x2b6a→0xc; 0x2ceb→0xb (continue) or 0x4fce (escape).

findings.claim: 0x2d6d is the state-0xa init-combat handler; 0x1d6a is the encounter-setup orchestrator; 0x024d is the per-encounter buffer reset.

evidence.details: 0x2d6d allocates 7 monster-group buffers (0x1a0 bytes each) + 7 monster-type buffers (0xde bytes each) + 12 animation slots (0x18 bytes each) via the 0xf4be arena thunk, creates the two combat windows via 0xbbb6 (left 0x13x0xb, right 0x14x0xa), calls 0x1d6a, optionally shows a 'surprise' message if 0x4fce==0x12 and >1 group, then transitions to state 0xb. 0x1d6a clears flags 0x43c8/0x43c6, sets 0x4354 if leader monster type matches scripted IDs (0x80/0x97/0x99), calls 0x024d (reset buffers), 0x0401 (spawn root monster group), 0x0f71 (initial xp tracking), 0x07f7 (load party into combat slots). 0x024d clears 0x4362 (rank matrix, 0x14 bytes), zeros all 7 group monster arrays (0x1a0 bytes each), resets count fields, sets 0x4358 (anim tick) to -2.

findings.claim: 0x0401 is the recursive monster-group spawn routine; 0x02c5 is the standard XdY+Z dice roller; 0x02f4 is a jump-table dispatcher (likely 'find zone for monster type').

evidence.details: 0x0401 takes (monster_type_id, group_slot): increments 0x4360 (group count), loads monster-type data via 0xc31e (the generic data-loader thunk) into *0x43b6[slot], stores type id at +0x19a of group's monster buffer, picks zone via 0x02f4, plays sound via 0x008d if type has a sound-id at +0xd2, rolls group size via 0x02c5 dice (with +/- adjustment based on 0x3593 ambush flag), clamps to 1..9, then per-monster: rolls HP via 0x02c5 on +0x78/+0x7a, rolls SP via 0x02c5 on +0x7c/+0x7e, sets rank=0xff (unassigned). At end, computes spawn cap from zone (363c+1)/2 + 1, rolls per-secondary-spawn (+0xa4/+0xa6) and recursively spawns into group_slot+1. 0x02c5 is `result = base + sum(rng(sides)+1 for _ in range(N))` — Wizardry's XdY+base. 0x02f4 reads a 12-entry table at 0x486f and jumps via piVar3[9] — a 12-case computed jump for monster-type → zone mapping.

findings.claim: 0x07f7 copies the party from the wmaze party struct array (0x43e8+i*0x1b0) into combat group 0's monster slots (0x43a8[0]+i*0x2c). 0x168f is the per-member writeback after combat.

evidence.details: 0x07f7 sets *0x43a8[0]+0x19d = *0x43ce (party size); zeros status-timer arrays at +0x18c (6 bytes) and +0x192 (4 bytes); for each party member i in 0..party_size-1, copies (HP, HP_max, SP_a, SP_a_max, SP_b, SP_b_max, status_level, 10-byte status flags, secondary_status_flag) from party struct fields at +0x4400/4402/4404/4406/440c/4589/450a/458c into combat slot fields at +0/+2/+4/+6/+8/+22/+e/+23. Sets +0x2a (rank) to 0xff. 0x168f does the inverse for ONE member: copies HP/SP/status back from combat slot to party struct. The 0x1b0 stride is identical to wmaze's party struct stride.

findings.claim: 0x2b6a is the state-0xb per-round driver; 0x2ceb is the state-0xe end-of-round handler.

evidence.details: 0x2b6a: iterates party members calling 0x1a82 (redraw_member_in_panel), calls 0x2692 (assign_monsters_to_rank_positions), calls 0x28ae(0) (animate 4 attack rounds), then if 0x5012==0 calls 0x11e7 (try_flee_combat); zeros 0x5012; sets 0x363a=0xc. 0x2ceb: calls 0x1716 (end-of-round resolve), 0x1086 (compact_groups), 0x0e66(6) (compact alive in some group), 0x2baf (decay status effects); if 0x4356 (combat-end flag) is set, writes back party via 0x168f loop, calls 0x2a52 (cleanup_windows), sets 0x363a = 0x4fce (return-to-caller state); else sets 0x363a=0xb (continue combat) and refreshes screen.

findings.claim: 0x205b is the animation-slot insert (sorted by depth); 0x215b is queue-attack-for-position; 0x23af plays one slot's animation frame; 0x27e9 advances the anim tick; 0x289d runs a full anim cycle.

evidence.details: 0x205b takes (depth_key, sprite_id, payload_bytes, target_byte, base_x, base_y, frame_bytes, str_ptr): finds insertion point in the 0..*0x438e sorted slot list at 0x4390[], memmoves later entries down, fills in new entry (+0x14 depth, +0x15 sprite, ptrs at +0/2/4/6, +0x16 frame_bytes), copies string via 0xf3aa, increments count. If 0x438e overflows 0xc, loops forever on 0xc546 (sound-loop). 0x215b reads 0x4362[rank][file] to find which group occupies position; rolls an attack table from monster type at +0x3750..+0x375c and queues via 0x205b. 0x23af: for slot i, if not erased (+0x14 != 0xff), checks monster type code at +0x432c; for type chars '\x14','#','6','9' iterates payload bytes calling 0xf10c (sprite blit) for each frame; otherwise single blit. 0x27e9: based on 0x4358 tick value: -3 = post-frame refresh via 0xf13c; -2 = call 0x44e8 (scene render) and reset slots to 0xff; -1 = iterate 2 ranks * 5 files calling 0x215b to queue attacks; 0..0xb = 0x23af on slot 0x4358. Increments 0x4358, wraps -3..0xb. 0x289d: sets 0x4358=-2, loops calling 0x27e9 until back to -2.

findings.claim: 0x2692 is the assign-monsters-to-rank-positions main loop; 0x2595/0x266b are the try-assign helpers; 0x0b02 assigns one monster to a specific rank/file with attack-target init.

evidence.details: 0x2692: for each rank (0..1) and each file via rng-permutation, looks up which group should claim that slot via 0x266b based on group count (1/2/3+ groups dictate which rank gets which); explicitly handles the case where 0x5010 (surprise flag) is 1 to force group at (0,0). 0x2595: takes (group_id, rank, file); finds first unassigned slot (+0x2a==0xff) in group, marks it assigned with rank*10+file, also marks 0x50b4 attack-flag and 0x4362 occupancy. 0x266b: starting from group `param_1`, calls 0x2595; if fails (returned non-zero), retries with group+1 up to group 3 (i.e. backoff up the group list). 0x0b02 iterates all assigned monsters in a group and computes which rank/file each one occupies based on its prior position, calls 0x099e to roll attacks for monsters in front rank only.

findings.claim: 0x099e rolls attack-target lookups for one group's monsters; 0x1dc2 is the per-monster attack-target picker.

evidence.details: 0x099e: for slot 0..count-1, reads monster-type's attack-data tables at +0x3732/+0x373c (base+dice), +0x3746/+0x3750 (target rank base+dice), +0x375b/+0x375c (target-flag base+dice). Stores results in the per-rank/file attack lookup at 0x3648/0x3649/0x364a (3-byte stride). Special-cases monster type '6' for slot 0. 0x1dc2: takes (group_id, attack_slot, output_buffer). For one monster's attack at a given slot, reads target IDs from the same +0x3648..+0x364a arrays, applies a counter at +0x3649 to walk through cycle, and writes attack-target list to output_buffer.

findings.claim: 0x0c8c is the per-slot status-effect tick (HP regen, damage, decay); 0x0e66 is compact-alive-in-group; 0x0f2f is the skill-levelup-on-hit roll; 0x0f71 is post-encounter xp-and-treasure award; 0x2baf is decay-per-group-status-effects.

evidence.details: 0x0c8c: takes (group_id, slot_idx, damage_in, defense_in). If 'attacking' flag (+0x10) set, rolls poison-tick via rng. Subtracts (damage - defense - armor_at_+0x23) from HP at +0x2; on HP<=0 sets death flag at +0x22=3, clears rank, clears 0x50b4 attack flag, and if monster has 'on-death' bit at +0xdc bit 0 calls 0xe31d (setbit) to flag an event. Iterates 10 status-timer slots at +0xe..+0x17 decrementing each. Returns 1 if died. 0x0e66: iterates group, calls 0x0c8c per slot with attack_in from monster type +0xd7, then bubbles surviving slots to front and updates count at +0x19d. 0x0f2f: rolls rng(skill_val at +0x451c); if rolled <= HP_max*N, increments skill value. 0x0f71: iterates groups, per party-member rolls rng(100) against thresholds at member+0x4533 (zone-modified by 0x363c) and +0x4515; on match clears 'has-attacked' flag and rolls XP/treasure via 0x0f2f. 0x2baf: iterates 7 groups, 6 status-timer types at +0x18c, 4 at +0x192, decrements each by max(1, decay_amt); also handles party-wide marker at 0x4ed8/0x4eda.

1192 bytes — a high-complexity function. Iterates groups, computes per-group 'speed sum' from per-slot HP/4 (excluding stunned at +0x22/+0x10/+0x11). Modifies via group-type +0xa8/+0xaa/+0xab speed bytes. Then iterates groups 0x4360..2, rolls rng on each group's flee-chance, on success: refreshes screen, calls FUN_42 (delay), formats a flee message using msg IDs 0xdb6 ('Group flees!') or 0xdb7 ('You all flee!'), positions the cursor centered, prints via 0xdf85, plays sound. Then swaps the fleeing group's pointers with group_count-1, calls 0x4dc2 (swap_bytes) to swap data, decrements 0x4360, and updates everything via 0x1010/0x0b02/0x2692/0x28ae. The 0xdb6/0xdb7/0xdb8 message ids are the smoking gun: those are the standard Wiz6 flee messages.

findings.claim: 0x1716 is the end-of-round resolve: applies per-member status updates, writes back to party struct, re-sorts party by status_level (alive first), checks for party wipe or all-fled.

evidence.details: Iterates 0..party_size-1: if status_level<3 (alive/stunned), calls 0x0c8c with monster_type's poison-damage values (+0x458a/+0x458b); on 'died this round' (==1), calls 0x1a82 to redraw the death animation, plays sound via 0xc546 with sound-id at +0x4586, writes the post-death party box. Then for each member calls 0x168f to write back to party struct. Then bubble-sort party by +0x4589 (status_level): swaps 0x1b0 bytes (full party struct) + 0x2c bytes (combat slot) + 2 secondary pointers via 0x4dc2. Then counts members with status_level>=2: if all = party_size, sets 0x4fce=8 (party-dead state) and 0x4356=1 (combat-end flag); also checks +0x2b==2 (all-fled flag), if so 0x4fce=0x17 + 0x4356=1.

findings.claim: 0x1086 is compact-and-check-end-of-combat: removes empty groups, transfers special groups, sets combat-end if all groups dead.

evidence.details: Iterates groups 1..0x4360 calling 0x0e66 on each (compact alive in group). If group survives, copies it to its new compacted index (group i → group local_8 if local_8<i). Special-cases two rank codes ('\v'=11 and '\f'=12) — those are 'summoned-creature' markers; on first sighting per combat the corresponding flag at 0x4368 / 0x436a is set and a 'replacement' attack-roll is queued via 0x099e. After compaction, sets 0x4360=local_8. If 0x4360==0 and 0x4fce!=8, sets 0x4fce=0xf (victory state) and 0x4356=1 (combat-end). Then calls 0x1010 (refresh monster zone links) and 0x0f71 (xp rolls).

findings.claim: 0x008d loads a SOUND%02d.SND file; 0x0169 loads a video-driver descriptor file (uses video_driver_thunk_0 at end).

evidence.details: 0x008d: param_1 = sound id. Writes id to 0x4336 (current sound). Calls 0xf0dc (pre-input disk check), builds filename via 0xc772 (boot_build_prompt_message — the 'load file by template' helper) with the printf-style number-to-ASCII via 'param_1/10+"0"', opens via 0xf924 (crt_open), reads via 0xee85 (huffman_load_and_decompress), and closes via 0xfda5 (crt_dos_close). Aborts via 0xbb71 on open/read failure. 0x0169 is the same pattern but for sprite descriptors (extension changes — references +0x36de/+0x36e2/+0x36e4 video-driver tables, and the final call after read is 0xf100, not the sound thunk).

findings.claim: 0x44e8 is the 3D combat-scene viewport renderer (2192 bytes); 0x4426 is the all-status-panels render dispatch; 0x3a7d/0x3fc5/0x41b4 are per-depth wall/door descriptor emitters; 0x42a3/0x4306/0x4337/0x4368/0x4395/0x43c7/0x43f9 are per-depth render-bit clearers.

evidence.details: 0x44e8: 2192 bytes (matches wmaze's view renderer in size). Saves party position (0x4fa0..0x4f9c), checks 0x43a (pit) bit: if set and zone is 0/4/5 calls 0x4426 (status-only render). Otherwise: zeros 7 per-depth flag bit-arrays at 0x513e/0x511a/0x5182/0x5126/0x518e/0x51a8 via 0xf34c. Iterates depth 0..4 (0x52f6 default 4): calls 0x3239 (front-wall check), 0x3622 (left-wall), 0x37df (right-wall), and dispatches to 0x3a7d (paint front-wall descriptors), 0x3fc5 (paint side walls), 0x41b4 (paint corners), each followed by a per-depth flag-clearer (0x42a3..0x43f9). After all depths drawn, iterates 0x51a6 monster-placement records (at 0x51a8, 11-byte stride: sprite ptrs + position + depth idx + state byte) calling 0xf148 (video_descriptor_render) to draw each monster sprite. Finally calls 0x4426 (status panels). 0x4426 iterates 6 status icons via jump table at -0x760e (a CS-relative offset), then status timers at 0x4ec8+i*4, then calls 0xf13c (post-frame refresh). 0x3a7d/0x3fc5/0x41b4 each take a depth + facing + sprite-ID args and call 0xf148 to blit. 0x42a3..0x43f9 each clear specific bits in the depth flag arrays after a piece has been drawn.

findings.claim: 0x2f8b, 0x2fc8, 0x30ee, 0x3153, 0x31b8 are byte-equivalent maze-walk helpers reused from wmaze.ovr's wall-check logic, used by the combat-scene renderer to draw the dungeon view behind the monster sprites.

evidence.details: 0x2f8b: facing-covers-xy check — returns -1 if (gy,gx) not in facing's 8x8 zone window; identical pattern to wmaze 0x357a. 0x2fc8: resolve global (x,y) to (zone-local x,y,facing) by trying current facing first, then cached fwd, then loops all 12 facings; identical to wmaze 0x35b7. 0x30ee/0x3153: dual wall-check primitives — both call 0x2fc8 then read bit-field at 0x4faa+0x60 (north walls) or 0x4faa+0x120 (west walls) respectively via getbits_n. 0x31b8: takes (xptr,yptr,faceptr,...,dx,dy) and applies the dx/dy in the appropriate axis based on current 4-direction facing 0x4f9a, then resolves to zone via 0x2fc8. These are all conceptually the same as wmaze's view_step_forward_by_facing (0x37a7) etc.

findings.claim: 0x3239 / 0x3622 / 0x37df are the front-wall / left-wall / right-wall checkers for the combat-scene viewport — each tests for pit/special-bit, then dispatches the actual N/W-wall lookup based on facing, then checks per-cell door state and special-square triggers.

evidence.details: All three: optionally apply offset via 0x31b8, compute cell index = z*0x40+y*8+x, getbit_test at +0x43a (pit) → if set AND zone<0xe, dispatch via jumptable at 0x793d (16 zone-specific handlers). getbit_test at +0x49a (some other event) → if set AND zone<0xe, dispatch via 0x7993. Then read walls via getbits_n based on facing 0..3 (each function rotates which wall offset to use — front uses +0x60/+0x120 in order 0,1,2,3; left rotates by one; right by two). Read +0x1f8 (special-square idx, 4 bits) and +0x378 (door state, 2 bits); on certain combinations dispatch via 0x7b3a/0x7d17/0x7ed6 (16-entry tables of zone-specific handlers). The triple cover the 3 walls visible at each depth in the 3-wide viewport.

findings.claim: 0x2a52 destroys all combat UI windows and frees descriptor structs (party portrait windows + combat panels + sprite slots).

evidence.details: Calls 0xbd6e (ui_window_destroy) on 0x438a and 0x438c (the two combat windows); 0xec6d (unfocus) on 0x3342 and 0x4fb2 and an unnamed window; 0xc497 (redraw_focused); 0xebb4 (focus); 0xed5a (clear) on the main window; then 5x putchar (drawing blank corners?) at the bottom row. Then 0xf5bc (free_struct) 14 times (7*2) for the monster-group struct buffers, and 12 more times for the sprite slots.

findings.claim: 0x1a82 redraws one party member in their portrait window; 0x1971 draws a right-aligned 2-digit stat number.

evidence.details: 0x1a82: takes member_idx. Picks window 0x4fba (even slots) or 0x4fb8 (odd) — the two party-portrait windows. Computes per-member yoffset = (idx/2)*4. Writes member name via 0xdfb9 (puts) + spaces. Iterates 3 cols * 3 rows drawing a 3x3 portrait grid of glyphs (via 0xde7f putchar). Computes status-level icon via lookup table at 0x526 (status sprites). Draws 2-byte equipment/weapon icons. Calls 0x1971 twice for HP and SP printouts at right-aligned positions. 0x1971: takes (window, x, y, value, max, color). Computes 3-digit decimal from value (offset trick: tens, units, with carry rotation). Calls 0xbda7 (set cursor) + 0xde7f for each digit.

findings.claim: 0x0042 delays N*10 ticks with keyboard-break; 0x4dc2 swaps two byte arrays of length N in place; 0x1010 refreshes monster-type-to-zone mapping after group changes.

evidence.details: 0x0042: flushes kbd, multiplies param by 10, loops while ticks>0 calling 0x27e9 (animation tick) and decrementing; exits early on mouse press, ENTER keypress, or other keys. The mouse-and-keyboard break pattern matches wmaze 0xdd7 (delay_with_keypress_poll). 0x4dc2: classic LOCKed byte-swap of arrays — XCHG-like memswap. 37 bytes. 0x1010: clears 0x4326..0x4328 (round-marker?), iterates groups 1..0x4360 recomputing each group's zone via 0x02f4 (find_zone_for_monster_type); also checks if leader monster has a sound id and plays it via 0x008d on type-change.

operational_notes.key_quirk: wmele.ovr is loaded with BinaryLoader (no MZ header), so file offset == Ghidra address. Cross-overlay calls go through BSS function-pointer thunks; the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset) resolved all 44 thunks deterministically. The project path symlinks the worktree's tools/ghidra/ to the canonical /Users/nathan/Projects/ndouglas/wiz6/tools/ghidra/, but PyGhidra rejects paths containing '.config' (leading-dot directories) so scripts must use the canonical path explicitly.
operational_notes.address_translation: wmele.ovr Ghidra addr == file offset (BinaryLoader); no 0x200 or 0x10000 adjustment needed. Cross-overlay thunk: subtract 0xBA9C from bss_offset to get wroot file offset (which in wroot.exe Ghidra terms is wroot_ghidra_addr - 0x10000).
